ABOUT

ABOUT MOTO RUSH

  • Moto Rush is an endless traffic-riding game. Weave through busy highway traffic on a superbike, chase the longest distance and beat your best score.
  • It runs fully in the browser with 3D graphics, so it works on phones and computers with nothing to install.
  • The ride never ends on its own: the bike keeps getting faster and the traffic keeps getting denser until you crash.

FEATURES

  • 4 bikes to unlock: Ninja H2R, BMW S1000RR, Aventor and Akira Bike, each with its own top speed and exhaust flame.
  • 6 places that change as you ride: Highway, River bridge, Night, Morning city, Desert and Snowfield.
  • Night ride with working street lamps and headlights on every car and on your bike.
  • Three camera views: chase, close and rider.
  • Realistic engine sound that follows your gears, plus vibration on close calls and crashes.
  • Your best scores and unlocked bikes are saved on your device.

GOAL

  • Ride as far as you can through the traffic. Your score grows with the distance you cover.

CONTROLS

  • Touch and hold anywhere on the screen to throttle. Let go and the bike slows down to a cruising speed.
  • Swipe left or right while holding to change lane. A short swipe moves one lane, a long swipe moves two lanes.
  • On a keyboard: Left / Right arrows (or A / D) change lane and Space is the throttle.
  • Camera: tap the camera button (or press C) to cycle between three views. Chase is the far view from behind, Close sits right behind the bike and follows it from lane to lane, and Rider is mounted at the front of the bike, so no bike parts block the road.

SCORE

  • While the throttle is held, the score multiplier climbs from x1.0 up to your bike's maximum (Ninja H2R x2.5, BMW S1000RR x3.5, Aventor x4.5, Akira Bike x5). It drops back to x1.0 when you release.
  • Close call: pass very close to a car without touching it and you get a +50 bonus.

TRAFFIC AND CRASHES

  • Cars flash an amber indicator for about a second before they change lane. Watch the blinkers.
  • Hitting a car ends the ride.
  • Leaving the edge of the road also ends the ride, so do not swipe out of the outer lanes.

SPEED AND PLACES

  • The top speed rises every 400 m of distance and the traffic gets denser as you go.
  • Every 800 m the scenery changes: Highway, River bridge, Night, Morning city, Desert and Snowfield. At night the street lamps switch on and every car and your bike turn on their headlights.

BIKES

    SETTINGS

    • Sound and vibration can be switched on or off from the Settings button. Vibration is used for close calls and crashes.

    TIPS

    • Do not hold the throttle all the time. Release it to slow down before a tight gap, then open it up again.
    • Watch the amber blinkers: a car that is signalling is about to move into your lane.
    • The multiplier only grows while you hold the throttle, so a long clear stretch is the best time to score.
